solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Further busy folk including James, for one

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bees are proverbially busy, so they are the busy folk
Sid James was a British comic actor, star of the Carry On films

explanation.surface: Adding to a list: more busy people, among them someone called James.
explanation.walkthrough: 'James, for one' points to a person whose surname is James; the setter wants his first name. Sid James was a well-known British comedy actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means in addition or moreover, exactly as 'further' can open a sentence.

clue.text: Insect, note, crossing line in pursuit of another

indicators.note: something in pursuit comes behind, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: another insect, following on from the definition

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so one piece spans and encloses the next

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A description of a bug and a musical note chasing each other across a stave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition must be read first: once the answer is an insect, 'another' means a second insect, which leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a hard-winged member of the largest order of creatures with six legs, so it is an example.

clue.text: Polish expert finds fish

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth or polish it
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist in polishing, or a Polish specialist, turns up a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P tempts you to read 'Polish' as the nationality; at the start of the clue it is simply the verb to polish. A dab hand is British for someone skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dab is a small flatfish of the flounder family found in shallow coastal waters.

clue.text: Pretend I'm blessed in action

indicators.note: things in action are moving about, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims to feel blessed while at work, perhaps without meaning it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the fodder is ignored; nine letters rearrange completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to hide true feelings behind a false front, which is a way of putting on an act.

clue.text: Dispatch poverty? Not difficult

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to take a word away, leaving only what remains

parts.note: hardship is want or poverty
hard means difficult; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Getting rid of poverty, the clue suggests, is easy enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it sound like a policy proposal; really 'Not difficult' strips the front off a longer word for poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to send them off by post or carrier, the same as dispatching them.

clue.text: That's disgusting about getting fingerprints on jimjams

indicators.note: one piece getting another simply acquires it alongside, so they join in sequence
'about' means turned round, as in an about-turn, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of disgust
dabs is British slang for fingerprints

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at finding grubby fingerprints on their pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimjams looks like British slang for pyjamas, but it also means a fit of nerves, and that is the definition. The habdabs (as in 'the screaming habdabs') is British slang for a state of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a fit of nervous jitters or anxiety, so one slang term replaces the other.

clue.text: Case, not the first to pursue small fiends

indicators.note: without its first, a word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a shell is a case or casing; it loses its opening letter
to hound someone is to pursue them
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An investigator is off the case, no longer leading the chase after little devils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case, not the first' reads like a detective losing a case; it is SHELL losing its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellhounds are demonic dogs of legend, and more loosely wicked people, so they are devils or fiends.

clue.text: British language not appearing initially in House

indicators.note: whatever is absent at the start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
lingo is an informal word for a language; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A British tongue is missing from the start of proceedings in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes 'House' look like Parliament; it is the game of house, or housey-housey, an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is the older British name for the numbers game played for prizes, the same game.

clue.text: When French director once, caught changing

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Jacques Tati was a French film director, now dead
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Recalling a time when a French director was caught in the middle of a change.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati made Monsieur Hulot's Holiday; 'once' marks him as a figure of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatic means not static, unstable or tending to shift position, so it describes something that keeps altering.

clue.text: Arguably, one proving journalist is clean?

parts.note: surface padding: it admits the next phrase is a stretched, whimsical reading
someone who shows or demonstrates something could be called a shower
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter asks whether someone can prove that a journalist has clean hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arguably' flags that the setter is stretching a word: one who shows is a SHOW-ER, not the bathroom fitting. The question mark on the definition admits that being showered only suggests being clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has just washed under running water is fresh and scrubbed, so the state follows from the action.

clue.text: County town likens Lenin to rock

indicators.note: to rock is to shake or sway, so these letters are shaken into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A provincial town compares the Soviet leader to rock, perhaps granite or rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Enniskillen is the county town of Fermanagh in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county town is the administrative centre of a county, and this one serves Fermanagh in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Couple wanting anything from Yorkshire in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters travel backwards

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect, famously Yorkshire, for anything

explanation.surface: A retired pair wishing for any little thing from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech has owt for anything and nowt for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, and a pair has the number of members that follows one when counting.

clue.text: Boy with odd bits of ideas where girls may go

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the odd bits of a word are those in odd-numbered places: first, third, fifth

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word

explanation.surface: A boy full of half-formed notions about where the girls hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: The ladies is the British name for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is the women's lavatory, the room that women and girls, rather than men, are expected to use.

clue.text: Valve casing in Triumph dry in part

indicators.note: a casing is the outside shell, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: an actor's part is his role
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: Describes a valve housed inside a Triumph motorbike, kept partly dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph is a British motorcycle maker, which makes 'valve casing' look like engineering; 'casing' is really the instruction to keep the word's outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A throttle is the valve controlling the flow of fuel or air into an engine, so it is a kind of valve.

clue.text: Crikey: large commercial interrupting fine, heavenly musical

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Crikey!'
F stands for fine, as on pencils and nibs
airy means of the air or sky, ethereal
L is the abbreviation for large
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a huge advert breaking into a fine, divine show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine, heavenly' reads as one description, but splits as F plus AIRY, and the large commercial goes into AIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: My Fair Lady is the Lerner and Loewe stage show based on Shaw's Pygmalion, a famous musical.

clue.text: Job done en bloc by us and our shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A task completed all together by a team working one shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our shift' sounds like a work rota, but 'shift' is the anagram signal. The phrase is a British way of saying 'and there you are'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when something is completed easily and simply, meaning that is all there is to it.

clue.text: Istanbul releasing first unusual list around capital

indicators.note: turned around, the letters run the other way
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order
to release something is to let it go, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
1st written with I for 1; these letters are removed
a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Istanbul gives up its leading position in a strange ranking of cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is 1ST, with the numeral read as I, which Istanbul happens to begin with. What remains is jumbled and the rota is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulan Bator, now usually Ulaanbaatar, is the capital city of Mongolia.

clue.text: Gym shoes picked up European variant of flu — you'd get this from spitting

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: daps is West Country and Welsh dialect for plimsolls, cheap canvas gym shoes

indicators.note: a variant is an altered version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spluttering description of flu picked up in a changing room, spread by spitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about coughing and spitting germs; in gardening, a spit is a spade's depth of soil, so digging a spit lifts a load of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the depth of one spade blade, so spitting, digging to that depth, brings up one blade-load of soil.

clue.text: Spread nap out in hide streaked with grey

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's hide

indicators.note: 'out' suggests things put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay out the pile of an animal skin that has grey streaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like the instruction to lay the nap out, but both words are the fodder, and 'out' shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or cloth described this way is flecked with dark and light, like mixed ground seasoning, especially greying hair.

clue.text: Basque sport curtailed in contact with pack from another

indicators.note: to curtail is literally to dock the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: pelota is the Basque court game played with a ball against a wall; it loses its last letter
on can mean touching, in contact with

explanation.surface: A Basque game, cut short, is linked with a team from some other sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From another' says the pack belongs to another sport: the peloton is the main bunch of riders in a cycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: In cycle racing the peloton is the large main group of riders, a pack drawn from road cycling rather than rugby.

clue.text: University, primarily for effect, pursuing biting hypocrite

indicators.note: what pursues comes behind, so these pieces follow the other one

parts.note: a tart remark is a sharp, biting one
U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only initial letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A university seems to be putting on a show, chasing some two-faced critic.
explanation.walkthrough: Molière's play Tartuffe (also spelt Tartufe) gave its name to a religious hypocrite; the name is now a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Molière's comedy is a pious fraud, so his name became a byword for a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Rowan eg may be so difficult

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rowan is a tree, and tree wood can be full of knots
second meaning: hard to solve, as in a tangled problem

explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rowan look like a person's name, such as Rowan Atkinson; here it is the mountain ash tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber with many knots is literally gnarled, and a problem that is tangled and hard to unpick is figuratively so.

clue.text: Slow Conservative hotline maybe deleting its first answer

indicators.note: deleting means removing, and 'its first' limits the removal to the earliest occurrence

parts.note: a jokey phone service in the style of Dial-a-Ride, one that connects you to a Tory
A is the abbreviation for answer; the first one is removed

explanation.surface: A slow Tory helpline that loses its first answer, like any call centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter invents a service called Dial-a-Tory, hence 'maybe'. Remove its first A and the rest stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means tending to delay or waste time, so someone dilatory is sluggish and tardy.

clue.text: New Year abroad, touring centre of prohibited region

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Celebrating New Year overseas by touring the heart of a forbidden land.
explanation.walkthrough: Tibet was long closed to foreigners, so 'prohibited region' fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is an autonomous area of China on the high plateau north of the Himalayas, so it is a region.

clue.text: Satellite towns regularly visited east of Gong River

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so these letters come after the rest

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE
R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: letters two and four of the word

explanation.surface: A travel note: satellite towns along a river called the Gong visited in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite towns' reads as one phrase meaning dormitory suburbs, but 'Satellite' is the definition by itself. The OBE is an order of the British Empire honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the larger moons of the planet Uranus, named after the fairy king in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Burden at the expense of The Times?

parts.note: 'on' can mean paid for by, as in 'drinks are on me'
the newspaper speaking of itself says 'us'

explanation.surface: A cost of some kind to be borne by The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the setter's own paper is being cast as 'we', so a treat paid by The Times is on us.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility that someone must carry, a load laid on them.

clue.text: Thick part of disc

definitions.meaning: first meaning: broad, plump, not thin
second meaning: the file allocation table that indexes a computer disk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of disc' invites a search for letters hidden in 'of disc', but none spell a word for thick; the part is the FAT, a disk's file allocation table.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something wide or plump, and the computing acronym names the index table on formatted storage.

clue.text: Experts using second-rate checks tied up when caught?

parts.note: B grade is second class

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so these pieces are taken by their sound

parts.note: reins check a horse; the word sounds like wet weather
trussed means tied up, as a chicken for roasting

explanation.surface: Specialists relying on shoddy restraints that tied someone up, perhaps a captured prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests being captured, but here it means heard. A brains trust is a British name for a panel answering questions, after a wartime BBC radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: A brains trust is a group of expert advisers, or a panel of knowledgeable people who answer questions in public.

clue.text: Tedious stretch before Fourth of July

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next

parts.note: a stretch of road or time is a length

indicators.note: the fourth of a word is its letter in fourth position

parts.note: the fourth letter of the month

explanation.surface: A dull wait in the run-up to American Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth of July' reads as the American holiday; taken literally it is the fourth letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lengthy goes on too long, and so becomes tiresome and dull, which is what tedious describes.

clue.text: One pressing to stop extremely smarmy MP's consultation

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills the middle of another
'extremely' points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
an urger is one who presses or urges

explanation.surface: A lobbyist insists on halting a greasy politician's meeting with voters.
explanation.walkthrough: A surgery is also a British MP's regular session where constituents come to raise problems in person.
explanation.definitionFit: British MPs hold regular surgeries in their constituency, sessions at which local voters can bring problems for advice.
